problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+(z+2)^{2}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$

feedback.problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}+\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{5}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the ellipsoid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}+\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{5} & =1 \\ (z+1)^{2} & =5(1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}-{y}^{2}) \\ z+1 & =\pm \sqrt{5(1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}-{y}^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}-{y}^{2}\ge 0 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the interior of the ellipse $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}=1$ and its boundary. 

Therefore, the domain is 

$$
{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}\le 1}.
$$
